title: Limit Laws for Extremal Quantile Regression at the Face of a Two-Power Benchmark
banked_reason: Sound regular and positive-finite critical QR laws; all-intermediate-sequence deliverable remains open. paper_score_ceiling 6.0 < 7.4 field floor; no bounded faithful D0 repair remains.
gap_reasons: The headline all-intermediate-sequence deliverable is not yet supplied: the actual ordinary-QR coefficient law, process topology, and calibration route for gamma_n -> 0 remain expressly open, so the delivered regular and positive-finite-critical results are a narrower kernel than promised.

proof_attempt_summary: Three constructive D0 rounds established the sharp Gaussian/relative-consistency boundary, positive-finite critical coefficient refinements, clipped face/interior laws, and padded pointwise calibration on the unchanged exact class and original QR rule. Four classical source statements were retrieved and attested; the final mathematical panel passed, but the achieved incremental package scored 6.0 below the field cutoff 7.4. The actual vanishing-scale estimator law, uniform critical process topology, and all-sequence calibration require new theory and remain explicitly open; no F stage or Lean proof was attempted.
tldr: For the original minimum-norm ordinary QR rule in the exact two-power benchmark, \(\kappa_n\to\infty\) is the sharp boundary for both the stated Gaussian coefficient law and relative-intercept consistency, with Gaussian moving-face/interior profile laws and feasible 90 percent pointwise intervals. When \(\gamma_n=p_n\sqrt{K_n}\log(1/p_n)\to g\in(0,\infty)\), the proved finite-dimensional projected-intercept/Gaussian-slope law and its signed/logarithmic refinements now yield fixed-point clipped moving-face and Gaussian positive-interior laws, together with learned-coefficient padded pointwise intervals. Vanishing-scale laws, infinite-dimensional critical mapping and inference across all nonregular sequences remain open. The conditional education-wage extreme-QTE workflow is a prospective consumer; no exact-family fit to NLSY79 is asserted.
gap: Chernozhukov (2005), Theorem 5.1, and Chernozhukov--Fernandez-Val (2011), Theorem 1, inform ordinary extremal QR under positive tail equivalence. Neither evaluates the singular profiled-loss transition in the exact two-power zero-face benchmark. Wang, Cai, Wang, Shi and Tang (2026), Theorems 1--2, distinguishes score convergence from coefficient inversion; its positive-scale coefficient results do not settle the sharp relative-intercept Gaussian frontier or its non-Gaussian replacement here.
fill: The focal sharp-frontier obligation derives both the primitive Gaussian-validity boundary and explicit alternative non-Gaussian objective/process laws for the unchanged ordinary QR rule throughout all intermediate sequences. Joint moving-face and interior clipped logratio laws then validate original-record pointwise calibration in the benchmark, specifying when the consumer workflow can use Gaussian tail-QR uncertainty near a vanishing face.
